newsitem.title: UK: Chicago rally has little impact on Euro veg oils.
newsitem.headline: Chicago rally has little impact on Euro veg oils.

text.p: Higher Chicago soybean futures on the back of forecasts of rain in Brazil at the weekend had little impact at the close of the European vegetable oil market on Thursday.
"Buyers did not want to pay the higher prices we had already, so it was pointless sellers going any higher," said a trader.
Chicago soybean futures rallied on forecasts of rain in Brazil at the weekend which could slow the soybean harvest.
"They love a weather market in Chicago, but we don't have to follow it," said another trader.
Soft oils closed with soy oil 0.50 guilders up and rape oil 0.50 to one guilder higher, both unchanged from midday.
In thin trading Mar rape oil fetched 99 guilders a 100 kilos and May/Jul 101.50 guilders.
Palm oil was slightly up from midday with player anticipating higher prices in Malaysian if Chicago holds it's gain at the close.
Earlier palm oil prices in driven higher in Europe by a late rally in Malaysia, but traders said there was no fundamental reason for the rise.
"We've seen an upward correction after the recent falls, but nothing has fundamentally changed," said a trader.
Traders said palm oil should continue to fall owing to slow exports and a quicker recovery in output after the holidays than expected.
Crude palm oil CIF Europe closed $5 to $7.50 up after Mar traded at $572.50 and $575 during the afternoon.
Products finished $2.50 to $7.50 up with no further business reported.
Coconut oil closed with gains of $7.50 after Feb/Mar traded at $775, $777.50 and $780, Mar/Apr at $762.50 and $770, Apr/May at $760 and May/Jul at $750 a tonne CIF in mainly dealer trading.
Palmkernel oil, closed $5 higher in a tradeless marker.
